methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Stack Infrastructure says it’s moving forward with AI data center in Pittsylvania
signals.signal_reading: Stack Infrastructure's AI data center in Pittsylvania represents capital infrastructure flowing to rural Virginia, but without corresponding workforce development or deep AI capability building, this signals shallow concentrated infrastructure rather than distributed human capacity.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab explicitly targets leadership preparation for AI adoption across sectors, signaling potential for deep, peer-networked capability building in a mid-sized market outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly address the distribution question by building grassroots AI fluency through peer networks, representing bottom-up capability development rather than top-down platform delivery.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional scaffolding for distributed AI education and community impact beyond the university, potentially seeding deep capability across Richmond's diverse neighborhoods and sectors.

signals.title: AI Has Already Arrived in Roanoke’s Classrooms. Here’s What Parents, Students, and Workers Should Know. - The Roanoke Rambler
signals.signal_reading: AI already embedded in Roanoke classrooms signals rapid platform-mediated adoption across K-12, but the article's focus on what stakeholders 'should know' suggests shallow understanding accompanying broad distribution—classic shallow/distributed dynamics.
